Full CI log: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/38897334125/job/116960857967

---

### Thread 2 — `js/checkBugTestsPassed.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-16):
# checkBugTestsPassed: label-mode gates cannot see stage markers on the preferred direct-links path

🚨 **BLOCKING: `hasStage` reads `fields.labels`, but direct-linked TC stubs never carry labels in label mode**

`isBlockingTC` now routes through `tracker.hasStage(tc, ...)`, which in `'label'` mode decides from `tc.fields.labels`. On the **preferred** TC path of this agent the TC objects come from `findDirectLinkedTCs` (`js/checkBugTestsPassed.js:58`) — i.e. from `ticket.fields.issuelinks[].outwardIssue` of `getIssue(ticketKey)`. Jira returns those embedded issue stubs with a reduced field set (`summary`, `status`, `priority`, `issuetype` — **no `labels`**), so `hasStage` can never match a `stage_passed` / `stage_bug_to_fix` marker there and the TC keeps blocking the Bug: in a `'label'` deployment the bug-done-check keeps returning `waiting` — the exact silent-deadlock class this PR fixes, in the flow that completes Bugs.

The repo's own pre-existing fixture shape agrees: `makeTc()` in `test_checkBugTestsPassed.js` has no `labels`. The new gh-916 fixture `gh916DirectTc(key, status, labels)` **stuffs `labels` into the issuelinks stub** — data the real API does not return — which is why the new tests green-light this path.

Contrast: `checkStoryTestsPassed.findLinkedTCs` and `mergeStoryTestAutomationPR.fetchLinkedTestCases` were correctly given `fields: [..., 'labels']` in label mode; the ADO path is also safe (`adoSearchFields` always returns `System.Tags`). Only this direct path is broken (the `linkedIssues` fallback here works, since `searchIssues` without `fields` returns everything on Jira).

**Suggested fix** — when `tracker.stageFallback() === 'label'`, re-fetch direct-linked TCs individually (or via one `key in (...)` search) so `labels` are real:

```javascript
function findDirectLinkedTCs(ticket) {
    // ... existing stub collection ...
    if (tracker.stageFallback() === 'label' && tcs.length > 0) {
        return tcs.map(function (tc) {
            try { return tracker.getIssue(tc.key) || tc; } catch (e) { return tc; }
        });
    }
    return tcs;
}
```

And extend the gh-916 suite with a case whose mock returns the realistic label-less stub so the fallback is exercised.

*Default `'none'` mode is unaffected (status-only comparison), and label mode is still strictly better than pre-PR behaviour — but the PR description claims these gates recognise markers, which does not hold on this path.*

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-16):
# New suites missing their per-module run_<module>.json

💡 **SUGGESTION: add `run_moveToInTesting.json` / `run_moveToReadyForTesting.json`**

AGENTS.md ("Writing tests for new logic"): *create/extend a `test_<module>.js`, **add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one)**, and include it in `run_all.json`.* Every other suite in `js/unit-tests/` has its own `run_*.json` (e.g. `run_checkStoryTestsPassed.json`); the two new files are only listed in `run_all.json`, so they cannot be run (or included in pack selection) individually.

Fix: add the two small `run_*.json` files mirroring the existing ones (one test file each).

### Thread 4 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-16):
# stageKeyForStatusName: configured-status projects silently lose the fallback

💡 **SUGGESTION: resolve `rule.targetStatus` against configured statuses too**

`stageKeyForStatusName` matches `statuses[key] === statusName` using the **default** status names only. A project that customises `jira.statuses` (e.g. `READY_FOR_TESTING: 'ReadyForTest'`, `useConfiguredStatusesInQueries: true`) keeps the `sm.json` literal `targetStatus: "Ready For Testing"`, so the reverse lookup returns `null` and the SM falls back to a plain `moveToStatus` — on a restricted workflow the transition is rejected again and only the generic `⚠️ Status transition failed` warn remains (the marker is never written). Pre-existing behaviour, no regression — but the new fallback silently doesn't apply exactly where the `useConfiguredStatusesInQueries` projects need it most.

# gh-916: [IMPL] #910: route test-automation status moves/gates through stage-label fallback (backward compatible)

## Description

Implements #910, building on #907 (PR #914 — `moveToStatusOrMark` now sweeps every stale `stage_*` label, so `previousStageKey` is optional).

## Goal
On trackers whose workflow does not contain a Jira-style status (ADO Test Case: `Design`/`Ready`/`Closed`; PBI/Bug: `New`…`Done`), the test-automation pipeline must not silently no-op. Status moves must fall back to a `stage_<key>` label when `jira.stageFallback === 'label'`, and every gate/query that reads those statuses must also accept the label.

## Hard requirement: backward compatibility
- Default `stageFallback: 'none'` (and Jira/GitHub with real statuses): **identical behaviour and API calls as today** — same `moveToStatus` error handling, same JQL/WIQL text, no extra reads.
- No signature/return-shape changes of exported functions; existing config keys keep working; new behaviour is opt-in via `jira.stageFallback: 'label'` (already the existing switch).
- Existing unit tests must stay green unchanged except where they assert the old direct `moveToStatus` call — update those minimally.

## Plan (do it in small commits)
1. Add to `js/common/trackers.js` a helper `tracker.hasStage(ticket, stageKey, statusName)` → true when `ticket.status === statusName` **or** (label mode) the ticket carries `stageLabel(stageKey)`. No behaviour change in `'none'` mode.
2. Replace direct `tracker.moveToStatus(key, STATUS)` with `tracker.moveToStatusOrMark(key, STATUS, '<STAGE_KEY>')` (no `previousStageKey`) at the call sites listed in #910 where `STATUS` can be tag-only (`PASSED`, `FAILED`, `IN_REVIEW_PASSED`, `IN_REVIEW_FAILED`, `SKIPPED`, `IRRELEVANT`, `BUG_TO_FIX`, `IN_TESTING`, `READY_FOR_TESTING`, `MERGED`): `finishTestCasesGeneration`, `moveToInTesting`, `moveToReadyForTesting`, `prepareTestPRForReview`, `mergeStoryTestAutomationPR`, `postBugCreation`, `checkBugTestsPassed`, `postBulkBugsCreation`, `postStoryTestAutomationResults`, `postTestReworkResults`, `recoverStuckTestCase`, `checkBugToFixReady`, `recoverMergedPRTicket`, `checkTaskStoriesDone`, `recoverFailedTCBugStatus`, `postTestAutomationResults`, `unblockResolvedDependencies`, `retryMergePR`, `checkStoryTestsPassed`, `storyTestAutomationRework`, `postTestReviewComments`, `postMobileTestAutomationResults`, `triggerBitriseTestAutomation`. Leave moves to statuses that exist everywhere (e.g. `DONE`, `BLOCKED`, `IN_REWORK` already routed) as they are.
   - Where the caller currently does `try { moveToStatus } catch (e) { console.warn }`, keep the catch; `moveToStatusOrMark` only changes the outcome in label mode.
3. Gates that compare `status === statuses.X` (`checkStoryTestsPassed`, `checkBugTestsPassed`, `retryMergePR`, `prepareTestPRForReview`, `mergeStoryTestAutomationPR`) must use `hasStage(...)` so a label-marked ticket is recognised.
4. WIQL/JQL built from tag-only statuses (`createBugFixBatchEpic.js:121`: `status in ("Failed","Bug To Fix")` on Test Case) must use the existing `{stage.KEY:Literal}` placeholder (`configLoader.interpolateStagePlaceholders`, already used by SM rules) so it becomes `(status in (...) OR labels = 'stage_x')` / `([System.State] IN (...) OR [System.Tags] CONTAINS 'stage_x')`. In `'none'` mode the produced query string must be unchanged.
5. Fail loudly: when neither the move nor the marker works, `moveToStatusOrMark` already throws — make sure these call sites do not swallow it into a success log (`✅ Moved …` must only print when `result.moved || result.marked`).

## Tests
- Per migrated agent: `'none'` mode → exact old call + old messages; `'label'` mode with a rejecting tracker → label added, no throw, correct log.
- `hasStage` table tests; `createBugFixBatchEpic` query string equality in `'none'` mode and the OR-clause in `'label'` mode (Jira + ADO).
- `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` (or the node harness) — no new failures vs main.

name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json

# Quality gate — CRAP ratchet via crap4js, pinned like crap4dart in dmd.
#
# Threshold policy (owner 2026-09-28): the CRAP bar is NOT lowered to pass —
# the CURRENT measured maximum is fixed as the ratchet baseline, so the code
# can only improve. Baseline: 4879.8 (action/developTicketAndCreatePR.js,
# CC=116 @ 29.3% coverage). Improvements lower the max freely; any change
# that pushes the max ABOVE the baseline fails the gate.
#
# Tool pin: crap4js v0.8.1 by release tag (same discipline as dmd pinning
# crap4dart 0.9.5). Install from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js' package is an
# unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  # Ratchet baseline — the measured repo-wide maximum CRAP (see header).
  # Re-measure with the steps below; lower it when the code improves.
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '4879.8'
  CRAP4JS_REF: 'v0.8.1'

jobs:
  crap:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is

Hmm, think about thread 4 carefully. `stageKeyForStatusName(statusName)` looks up the DEFAULT `statuses` map (from projectConfig.jira.statuses — wait, what is projectConfig here? Let me check: `var statuses = (projectConfig && projectConfig.jira && projectConfig.jira.statuses) || {}`. So it reads the merged project config statuses. A project that customizes `jira.statuses.READY_FOR_TESTING: 'ReadyForTest'` gets `statuses['READY_FOR_TESTING'] = 'ReadyForTest'`, and sm.json's literal `targetStatus: "Ready For Testing"` no longer matches — returns null → plain move → on a restricted workflow, rejected with only a generic warn.

Wait, but how do the default statuses look? Let me check config.js STATUSES. The defaults are like `READY_FOR_TESTING: 'Ready For Testing'`. With `useConfiguredStatusesInQueries: true`, queries use configured values. If a project renames the status to 'ReadyForTest', then the sm.json rule's `targetStatus: 'Ready For Testing'` is stale even in the plain-move world — the move itself would fail ("Ready For Testing" doesn't exist in that project). Hmm, but the reviewer says "keeps the sm.json literal targetStatus: 'Ready For Testing', so the reverse lookup returns null and the SM falls back to a plain moveToStatus — on a restricted workflow the transition is rejected again".

Options given: (a) also try a case-insensitive match on the key-derived name; (b) document in sm.json that targetStatus must stay aligned with jira.statuses values when stage fallback is enabled.

What's the cheapest, safest fix that addresses the suggestion without scope creep? The reviewer marked it SUGGESTION ("Pre-existing behaviour, no regression"). Options:

Option A: Extend `stageKeyForStatusName` to fall back to the DEFAULT statuses from config.js when the configured lookup misses. I.e., match against `STATUSES[key]` (default names) too. That means for a configured-status project with `READY_FOR_TESTING: 'ReadyForTest'`, `stageKeyForStatusName('Ready For Testing')` returns 'READY_FOR_TESTING' via the default-name match, and the SM calls `moveToStatusOrMark(key, 'Ready For Testing', 'READY_FOR_TESTING')`. In label mode, if the transition of 'Ready For Testing' fails, the marker `stage_ready_for_testing` is written. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 921
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/921
- **Title**: gh-916 [IMPL] #910: route test-automation status moves/gates through stage-label fallback (backward compatible)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-916` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 49
- **Additions**: +1533
- **Deletions**: -154
- **Created**: 2026-10-16T11:58:29Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-16T12:33:53Z

## PR Description

Closes #916
### Root Cause

On restricted workflows (ADO Test Case / ADO PBI), the test-automation statuses (`Passed`, `Failed`, `In Review - Passed/Failed`, `Skipped`, `Irrelevant`, `Bug To Fix`, `In Testing`, `Ready For Testing`, `Merged`) are tag-only. ~25 modules moved tickets with raw `tracker.moveToStatus(...)`, so ADO rejected the transition and the call sites swallowed the error — no status change, no `stage_*` marker, and `✅ Moved …` logs that lied. The shipped SM rules made it worse: their JQL gated on the same statuses, so tickets carrying only a `stage_*` marker were invisible, and `smAgent`'s `rule.targetStatus` move (Merged → Ready For Testing) hit the same raw call.

### Fix

- `js/common/trackers.js`: added `hasStage(ticket, stageKey, statusName)` — status match, or (label mode only) the `stage_<key>` marker; no label reads in the default `'none'` mode.
- Migrated every test-automation mover to `moveToStatusOrMark(key, STATUS, STAGE_KEY)` (`moveToInTesting`, `moveToReadyForTesting`, `post*Results`, `mergeStoryTestAutomationPR`, `retryMergePR`, `prepareTestPRForReview`, `check*Passed`, `checkBugToFixReady`, `checkTaskStoriesDone`, `finishTestCasesGeneration`, `storyTestAutomationRework`, `triggerBitriseTestAutomation`, `recover*`, `postBugCreation`, `postBulkBugsCreation`, `createBugFixBatchEpic`); dev-flow statuses (Done, Blocked, In Rework, In Review, Backlog, …) stay direct moves.
- Status-equality gates in the check/merge/PR modules now resolve through `hasStage(...)`.
- `sm.json` (≡ `agents/sm.json`), `agents/sm_merge.json`, `agents/bulk_bugs_creation.json`: tag-only-status gates switched to whole-clause `{stage.X:Literal}` placeholders; in `'none'` mode single-status rules expand byte-identical, two-status rules to the equivalent `status in ('A') OR status in ('B')`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rule.targetStatus` resolves against the tag-only stage set and falls back to `moveToStatusOrMark`; `js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js` mirrors `testRunner.js`'s `makeDefaultConfigLoaderMock` helpers.

Opt-in via the existing `jira.stageFallback: 'label'` / `customParams.stageFallback`; default `'none'` keeps today's behaviour.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests per flow: rejected transitions in `'label'` mode now mark `stage_*` and the flow completes (e.g. `test_moveToInTesting`, `test_mergeStoryTestAutomationPR`, `test_retryMergePR`, `test_recoverMergedPRTicket`, `test_smAgent` targetStatus suites); `'none'`-mode tests pin the unchanged path.
- Full suite: 136 files from `run_all.json` — 2823 passed, 18 failed; all 18 verified pre-existing node-harness mock gaps (they fail identically at the pre-change commit `e48129c`, e.g. `file_list`/`assert.doesNotThrow` exist only in the GraalJS runner). No new failures; two `finishTestCasesGeneration` tests that already failed at `e48129c` now pass.

### Notes

- `agents/` here is a self-symlink (consumer-layout shim, gitignored) — `sm.json` and `agents/sm.json` are one file.
- Two-status `{stage.*}` rules expand to two OR-ed clauses instead of one two-value `status in (...)` — same selection, different bytes, in `'none'` mode too.
- One pre-existing node-harness failure in `test_smAgent.js` (`assert.doesNotThrow` exists only in the GraalJS runner) is unrelated.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

### Thread 2 — `js/checkBugTestsPassed.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-16):
# checkBugTestsPassed: label-mode gates cannot see stage markers on the preferred direct-links path

🚨 **BLOCKING: `hasStage` reads `fields.labels`, but direct-linked TC stubs never carry labels in label mode**

`isBlockingTC` now routes through `tracker.hasStage(tc, ...)`, which in `'label'` mode decides from `tc.fields.labels`. On the **preferred** TC path of this agent the TC objects come from `findDirectLinkedTCs` (`js/checkBugTestsPassed.js:58`) — i.e. from `ticket.fields.issuelinks[].outwardIssue` of `getIssue(ticketKey)`. Jira returns those embedded issue stubs with a reduced field set (`summary`, `status`, `priority`, `issuetype` — **no `labels`**), so `hasStage` can never match a `stage_passed` / `stage_bug_to_fix` marker there and the TC keeps blocking the Bug: in a `'label'` deployment the bug-done-check keeps returning `waiting` — the exact silent-deadlock class this PR fixes, in the flow that completes Bugs.

The repo's own pre-existing fixture shape agrees: `makeTc()` in `test_checkBugTestsPassed.js` has no `labels`. The new gh-916 fixture `gh916DirectTc(key, status, labels)` **stuffs `labels` into the issuelinks stub** — data the real API does not return — which is why the new tests green-light this path.

Contrast: `checkStoryTestsPassed.findLinkedTCs` and `mergeStoryTestAutomationPR.fetchLinkedTestCases` were correctly given `fields: [..., 'labels']` in label mode; the ADO path is also safe (`adoSearchFields` always returns `System.Tags`). Only this direct path is broken (the `linkedIssues` fallback here works, since `searchIssues` without `fields` returns everything on Jira).

**Suggested fix** — when `tracker.stageFallback() === 'label'`, re-fetch direct-linked TCs individually (or via one `key in (...)` search) so `labels` are real:

```javascript
function findDirectLinkedTCs(ticket) {
    // ... existing stub collection ...
    if (tracker.stageFallback() === 'label' && tcs.length > 0) {
        return tcs.map(function (tc) {
            try { return tracker.getIssue(tc.key) || tc; } catch (e) { return tc; }
        });
    }
    return tcs;
}
```

And extend the gh-916 suite with a case whose mock returns the realistic label-less stub so the fallback is exercised.

*Default `'none'` mode is unaffected (status-only comparison), and label mode is still strictly better than pre-PR behaviour — but the PR description claims these gates recognise markers, which does not hold on this path.*

💡 **SUGGESTION: add `run_moveToInTesting.json` / `run_moveToReadyForTesting.json`**

AGENTS.md ("Writing tests for new logic"): *create/extend a `test_<module>.js`, **add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one)**, and include it in `run_all.json`.* Every other suite in `js/unit-tests/` has its own `run_*.json` (e.g. `run_checkStoryTestsPassed.json`); the two new files are only listed in `run_all.json`, so they cannot be run (or included in pack selection) individually.

Fix: add the two small `run_*.json` files mirroring the existing ones (one test file each).

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-16):
# stageKeyForStatusName: configured-status projects silently lose the fallback

💡 **SUGGESTION: resolve `rule.targetStatus` against configured statuses too**

`stageKeyForStatusName` matches `statuses[key] === statusName` using the **default** status names only. A project that customises `jira.statuses` (e.g. `READY_FOR_TESTING: 'ReadyForTest'`, `useConfiguredStatusesInQueries: true`) keeps the `sm.json` literal `targetStatus: "Ready For Testing"`, so the reverse lookup returns `null` and the SM falls back to a plain `moveToStatus` — on a restricted workflow the transition is rejected again and only the generic `⚠️ Status transition failed` warn remains (the marker is never written). Pre-existing behaviour, no regression — but the new fallback silently doesn't apply exactly where the `useConfiguredStatusesInQueries` projects need it most.

# gh-916: [IMPL] #910: route test-automation status moves/gates through stage-label fallback (backward compatible)

## Description

Implements #910, building on #907 (PR #914 — `moveToStatusOrMark` now sweeps every stale `stage_*` label, so `previousStageKey` is optional).

## Goal
On trackers whose workflow does not contain a Jira-style status (ADO Test Case: `Design`/`Ready`/`Closed`; PBI/Bug: `New`…`Done`), the test-automation pipeline must not silently no-op. Status moves must fall back to a `stage_<key>` label when `jira.stageFallback === 'label'`, and every gate/query that reads those statuses must also accept the label.

## Hard requirement: backward compatibility
- Default `stageFallback: 'none'` (and Jira/GitHub with real statuses): **identical behaviour and API calls as today** — same `moveToStatus` error handling, same JQL/WIQL text, no extra reads.
- No signature/return-shape changes of exported functions; existing config keys keep working; new behaviour is opt-in via `jira.stageFallback: 'label'` (already the existing switch).
- Existing unit tests must stay green unchanged except where they assert the old direct `moveToStatus` call — update those minimally.

## Plan (do it in small commits)
1. Add to `js/common/trackers.js` a helper `tracker.hasStage(ticket, stageKey, statusName)` → true when `ticket.status === statusName` **or** (label mode) the ticket carries `stageLabel(stageKey)`. No behaviour change in `'none'` mode.
2. Replace direct `tracker.moveToStatus(key, STATUS)` with `tracker.moveToStatusOrMark(key, STATUS, '<STAGE_KEY>')` (no `previousStageKey`) at the call sites listed in #910 where `STATUS` can be tag-only (`PASSED`, `FAILED`, `IN_REVIEW_PASSED`, `IN_REVIEW_FAILED`, `SKIPPED`, `IRRELEVANT`, `BUG_TO_FIX`, `IN_TESTING`, `READY_FOR_TESTING`, `MERGED`): `finishTestCasesGeneration`, `moveToInTesting`, `moveToReadyForTesting`, `prepareTestPRForReview`, `mergeStoryTestAutomationPR`, `postBugCreation`, `checkBugTestsPassed`, `postBulkBugsCreation`, `postStoryTestAutomationResults`, `postTestReworkResults`, `recoverStuckTestCase`, `checkBugToFixReady`, `recoverMergedPRTicket`, `checkTaskStoriesDone`, `recoverFailedTCBugStatus`, `postTestAutomationResults`, `unblockResolvedDependencies`, `retryMergePR`, `checkStoryTestsPassed`, `storyTestAutomationRework`, `postTestReviewComments`, `postMobileTestAutomationResults`, `triggerBitriseTestAutomation`. Leave moves to statuses that exist everywhere (e.g. `DONE`, `BLOCKED`, `IN_REWORK` already routed) as they are.
   - Where the caller currently does `try { moveToStatus } catch (e) { console.warn }`, keep the catch; `moveToStatusOrMark` only changes the outcome in label mode.
3. Gates that compare `status === statuses.X` (`checkStoryTestsPassed`, `checkBugTestsPassed`, `retryMergePR`, `prepareTestPRForReview`, `mergeStoryTestAutomationPR`) must use `hasStage(...)` so a label-marked ticket is recognised.
4. WIQL/JQL built from tag-only statuses (`createBugFixBatchEpic.js:121`: `status in ("Failed","Bug To Fix")` on Test Case) must use the existing `{stage.KEY:Literal}` placeholder (`configLoader.interpolateStagePlaceholders`, already used by SM rules) so it becomes `(status in (...) OR labels = 'stage_x')` / `([System.State] IN (...) OR [System.Tags] CONTAINS 'stage_x')`. In `'none'` mode the produced query string must be unchanged.
5. Fail loudly: when neither the move nor the marker works, `moveToStatusOrMark` already throws — make sure these call sites do not swallow it into a success log (`✅ Moved …` must only print when `result.moved || result.marked`).

## Tests
- Per migrated agent: `'none'` mode → exact old call + old messages; `'label'` mode with a rejecting tracker → label added, no throw, correct log.
- `hasStage` table tests; `createBugFixBatchEpic` query string equality in `'none'` mode and the OR-clause in `'label'` mode (Jira + ADO).
- `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` (or the node harness) — no new failures vs main.

blocks.text:
name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json

# Quality gate — CRAP ratchet via crap4js, pinned like crap4dart in dmd.
#
# Threshold policy (owner 2026-09-28): the CRAP bar is NOT lowered to pass —
# the CURRENT measured maximum is fixed as the ratchet baseline, so the code
# can only improve. Baseline: 4879.8 (action/developTicketAndCreatePR.js,
# CC=116 @ 29.3% coverage). Improvements lower the max freely; any change
# that pushes the max ABOVE the baseline fails the gate.
#
# Tool pin: crap4js v0.8.1 by release tag (same discipline as dmd pinning
# crap4dart 0.9.5). Install from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js' package is an
# unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  # Ratchet baseline — the measured repo-wide maximum CRAP (see header).
  # Re-measure with the steps below; lower it when the code improves.
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '4879.8'
  CRAP4JS_REF: 'v0.8.1'

jobs:
  crap:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 921
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/921
- **Title**: gh-916 [IMPL] #910: route test-automation status moves/gates through stage-label fallback (backward compatible)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-916` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 49
- **Additions**: +1533
- **Deletions**: -154
- **Created**: 2026-10-16T11:58:29Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-16T12:33:53Z

## PR Description

Closes #916
### Root Cause

On restricted workflows (ADO Test Case / ADO PBI), the test-automation statuses (`Passed`, `Failed`, `In Review - Passed/Failed`, `Skipped`, `Irrelevant`, `Bug To Fix`, `In Testing`, `Ready For Testing`, `Merged`) are tag-only. ~25 modules moved tickets with raw `tracker.moveToStatus(...)`, so ADO rejected the transition and the call sites swallowed the error — no status change, no `stage_*` marker, and `✅ Moved …` logs that lied. The shipped SM rules made it worse: their JQL gated on the same statuses, so tickets carrying only a `stage_*` marker were invisible, and `smAgent`'s `rule.targetStatus` move (Merged → Ready For Testing) hit the same raw call.

### Fix

- `js/common/trackers.js`: added `hasStage(ticket, stageKey, statusName)` — status match, or (label mode only) the `stage_<key>` marker; no label reads in the default `'none'` mode.
- Migrated every test-automation mover to `moveToStatusOrMark(key, STATUS, STAGE_KEY)` (`moveToInTesting`, `moveToReadyForTesting`, `post*Results`, `mergeStoryTestAutomationPR`, `retryMergePR`, `prepareTestPRForReview`, `check*Passed`, `checkBugToFixReady`, `checkTaskStoriesDone`, `finishTestCasesGeneration`, `storyTestAutomationRework`, `triggerBitriseTestAutomation`, `recover*`, `postBugCreation`, `postBulkBugsCreation`, `createBugFixBatchEpic`); dev-flow statuses (Done, Blocked, In Rework, In Review, Backlog, …) stay direct moves.
- Status-equality gates in the check/merge/PR modules now resolve through `hasStage(...)`.
- `sm.json` (≡ `agents/sm.json`), `agents/sm_merge.json`, `agents/bulk_bugs_creation.json`: tag-only-status gates switched to whole-clause `{stage.X:Literal}` placeholders; in `'none'` mode single-status rules expand byte-identical, two-status rules to the equivalent `status in ('A') OR status in ('B')`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rule.targetStatus` resolves against the tag-only stage set and falls back to `moveToStatusOrMark`; `js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js` mirrors `testRunner.js`'s `makeDefaultConfigLoaderMock` helpers.

Opt-in via the existing `jira.stageFallback: 'label'` / `customParams.stageFallback`; default `'none'` keeps today's behaviour.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests per flow: rejected transitions in `'label'` mode now mark `stage_*` and the flow completes (e.g. `test_moveToInTesting`, `test_mergeStoryTestAutomationPR`, `test_retryMergePR`, `test_recoverMergedPRTicket`, `test_smAgent` targetStatus suites); `'none'`-mode tests pin the unchanged path.
- Full suite: 136 files from `run_all.json` — 2823 passed, 18 failed; all 18 verified pre-existing node-harness mock gaps (they fail identically at the pre-change commit `e48129c`, e.g. `file_list`/`assert.doesNotThrow` exist only in the GraalJS runner). No new failures; two `finishTestCasesGeneration` tests that already failed at `e48129c` now pass.

### Notes

- `agents/` here is a self-symlink (consumer-layout shim, gitignored) — `sm.json` and `agents/sm.json` are one file.
- Two-status `{stage.*}` rules expand to two OR-ed clauses instead of one two-value `status in (...)` — same selection, different bytes, in `'none'` mode too.
- One pre-existing node-harness failure in `test_smAgent.js` (`assert.doesNotThrow` exists only in the GraalJS runner) is unrelated.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #921._

> ℹ️ **1 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `bulk_bugs_creation.json`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-16):
# Stale generated docs — CI gate `docs-freshness` is red on head 378dfbd9

🚨 **BLOCKING: docs/agents/generated is stale — `docs-freshness` fails**

The PR changes `failedTCsJql` in `bulk_bugs_creation.json`, but the generated doc was not regenerated. Reproduced locally on head `378dfbd9`:

```
$ node js/agentDocGenerator.js
$ git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated
diff --git a/docs/agents/generated/bulk_bugs_creation.md b/docs/agents/generated/bulk_bugs_creation.md
--- a/docs/agents/generated/bulk_bugs_creation.md
+++ b/docs/agents/generated/bulk_bugs_creation.md
-- `failedTCsJql`: "... AND status = {status.FAILED:Failed} AND ..."
+- `failedTCsJql`: "... AND {stage.FAILED:Failed} AND ..."
```

`sm.json` is excluded from the generator (`js/agentDocGenerator.js:58`), so this is the only stale file.

**Fix:**

```bash
node js/agentDocGenerator.js
git add docs/agents/generated/bulk_bugs_creation.md
git commit
```

Full CI log: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/38897334125/job/116960857967

---

### Thread 2 — `js/checkBugTestsPassed.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-16):
# checkBugTestsPassed: label-mode gates cannot see stage markers on the preferred direct-links path

🚨 **BLOCKING: `hasStage` reads `fields.labels`, but direct-linked TC stubs never carry labels in label mode**

`isBlockingTC` now routes through `tracker.hasStage(tc, ...)`, which in `'label'` mode decides from `tc.fields.labels`. On the **preferred** TC path of this agent the TC objects come from `findDirectLinkedTCs` (`js/checkBugTestsPassed.js:58`) — i.e. from `ticket.fields.issuelinks[].outwardIssue` of `getIssue(ticketKey)`. Jira returns those embedded issue stubs with a reduced field set (`summary`, `status`, `priority`, `issuetype` — **no `labels`**), so `hasStage` can never match a `stage_passed` / `stage_bug_to_fix` marker there and the TC keeps blocking the Bug: in a `'label'` deployment the bug-done-check keeps returning `waiting` — the exact silent-deadlock class this PR fixes, in the flow that completes Bugs.

The repo's own pre-existing fixture shape agrees: `makeTc()` in `test_checkBugTestsPassed.js` has no `labels`. The new gh-916 fixture `gh916DirectTc(key, status, labels)` **stuffs `labels` into the issuelinks stub** — data the real API does not return — which is why the new tests green-light this path.

Contrast: `checkStoryTestsPassed.findLinkedTCs` and `mergeStoryTestAutomationPR.fetchLinkedTestCases` were correctly given `fields: [..., 'labels']` in label mode; the ADO path is also safe (`adoSearchFields` always returns `System.Tags`). Only this direct path is broken (the `linkedIssues` fallback here works, since `searchIssues` without `fields` returns everything on Jira).

**Suggested fix** — when `tracker.stageFallback() === 'label'`, re-fetch direct-linked TCs individually (or via one `key in (...)` search) so `labels` are real:

```javascript
function findDirectLinkedTCs(ticket) {
    // ... existing stub collection ...
    if (tracker.stageFallback() === 'label' && tcs.length > 0) {
        return tcs.map(function (tc) {
            try { return tracker.getIssue(tc.key) || tc; } catch (e) { return tc; }
        });
    }
    return tcs;
}
```

And extend the gh-916 suite with a case whose mock returns the realistic label-less stub so the fallback is exercised.

*Default `'none'` mode is unaffected (status-only comparison), and label mode is still strictly better than pre-PR behaviour — but the PR description claims these gates recognise markers, which does not hold on this path.*

---

### Thread 3 — `js/unit-tests/run_all.json`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-16):
# New suites missing their per-module run_<module>.json

💡 **SUGGESTION: add `run_moveToInTesting.json` / `run_moveToReadyForTesting.json`**

AGENTS.md ("Writing tests for new logic"): *create/extend a `test_<module>.js`, **add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one)**, and include it in `run_all.json`.* Every other suite in `js/unit-tests/` has its own `run_*.json` (e.g. `run_checkStoryTestsPassed.json`); the two new files are only listed in `run_all.json`, so they cannot be run (or included in pack selection) individually.

Fix: add the two small `run_*.json` files mirroring the existing ones (one test file each).

---

### Thread 4 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-16):
# stageKeyForStatusName: configured-status projects silently lose the fallback

💡 **SUGGESTION: resolve `rule.targetStatus` against configured statuses too**

`stageKeyForStatusName` matches `statuses[key] === statusName` using the **default** status names only. # gh-916: [IMPL] #910: route test-automation status moves/gates through stage-label fallback (backward compatible)

## Description

Implements #910, building on #907 (PR #914 — `moveToStatusOrMark` now sweeps every stale `stage_*` label, so `previousStageKey` is optional).

## Goal
On trackers whose workflow does not contain a Jira-style status (ADO Test Case: `Design`/`Ready`/`Closed`; PBI/Bug: `New`…`Done`), the test-automation pipeline must not silently no-op. Status moves must fall back to a `stage_<key>` label when `jira.stageFallback === 'label'`, and every gate/query that reads those statuses must also accept the label.

## Hard requirement: backward compatibility
- Default `stageFallback: 'none'` (and Jira/GitHub with real statuses): **identical behaviour and API calls as today** — same `moveToStatus` error handling, same JQL/WIQL text, no extra reads.
- No signature/return-shape changes of exported functions; existing config keys keep working; new behaviour is opt-in via `jira.stageFallback: 'label'` (already the existing switch).
- Existing unit tests must stay green unchanged except where they assert the old direct `moveToStatus` call — update those minimally.

## Plan (do it in small commits)
1. Add to `js/common/trackers.js` a helper `tracker.hasStage(ticket, stageKey, statusName)` → true when `ticket.status === statusName` **or** (label mode) the ticket carries `stageLabel(stageKey)`. No behaviour change in `'none'` mode.
2. Replace direct `tracker.moveToStatus(key, STATUS)` with `tracker.moveToStatusOrMark(key, STATUS, '<STAGE_KEY>')` (no `previousStageKey`) at the call sites listed in #910 where `STATUS` can be tag-only (`PASSED`, `FAILED`, `IN_REVIEW_PASSED`, `IN_REVIEW_FAILED`, `SKIPPED`, `IRRELEVANT`, `BUG_TO_FIX`, `IN_TESTING`, `READY_FOR_TESTING`, `MERGED`): `finishTestCasesGeneration`, `moveToInTesting`, `moveToReadyForTesting`, `prepareTestPRForReview`, `mergeStoryTestAutomationPR`, `postBugCreation`, `checkBugTestsPassed`, `postBulkBugsCreation`, `postStoryTestAutomationResults`, `postTestReworkResults`, `recoverStuckTestCase`, `checkBugToFixReady`, `recoverMergedPRTicket`, `checkTaskStoriesDone`, `recoverFailedTCBugStatus`, `postTestAutomationResults`, `unblockResolvedDependencies`, `retryMergePR`, `checkStoryTestsPassed`, `storyTestAutomationRework`, `postTestReviewComments`, `postMobileTestAutomationResults`, `triggerBitriseTestAutomation`. Leave moves to statuses that exist everywhere (e.g. `DONE`, `BLOCKED`, `IN_REWORK` already routed) as they are.
   - Where the caller currently does `try { moveToStatus } catch (e) { console.warn }`, keep the catch; `moveToStatusOrMark` only changes the outcome in label mode.
3. Gates that compare `status === statuses.X` (`checkStoryTestsPassed`, `checkBugTestsPassed`, `retryMergePR`, `prepareTestPRForReview`, `mergeStoryTestAutomationPR`) must use `hasStage(...)` so a label-marked ticket is recognised.
4. WIQL/JQL built from tag-only statuses (`createBugFixBatchEpic.js:121`: `status in ("Failed","Bug To Fix")` on Test Case) must use the existing `{stage.KEY:Literal}` placeholder (`configLoader.interpolateStagePlaceholders`, already used by SM rules) so it becomes `(status in (...) OR labels = 'stage_x')` / `([System.State] IN (...) OR [System.Tags] CONTAINS 'stage_x')`. In `'none'` mode the produced query string must be unchanged.
5. Fail loudly: when neither the move nor the marker works, `moveToStatusOrMark` already throws — make sure these call sites do not swallow it into a success log (`✅ Moved …` must only print when `result.moved || result.marked`).

## Tests
- Per migrated agent: `'none'` mode → exact old call + old messages; `'label'` mode with a rejecting tracker → label added, no throw, correct log.
- `hasStage` table tests; `createBugFixBatchEpic` query string equality in `'none'` mode and the OR-clause in `'label'` mode (Jira + ADO).
- `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` (or the node harness) — no new failures vs main.

blocks.text:
name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json

# Quality gate — CRAP ratchet via crap4js, pinned like crap4dart in dmd.
#
# Threshold policy (owner 2026-09-28): the CRAP bar is NOT lowered to pass —
# the CURRENT measured maximum is fixed as the ratchet baseline, so the code
# can only improve. Baseline: 4879.8 (action/developTicketAndCreatePR.js,
# CC=116 @ 29.3% coverage). Improvements lower the max freely; any change
# that pushes the max ABOVE the baseline fails the gate.
#
# Tool pin: crap4js v0.8.1 by release tag (same discipline as dmd pinning
# crap4dart 0.9.5). Install from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js' package is an
# unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  # Ratchet baseline — the measured repo-wide maximum CRAP (see header).
  # Re-measure with the steps below; lower it when the code improves.
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '4879.8'
  CRAP4JS_REF: 'v0.8.1'

jobs:
  crap:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 921
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/921
- **Title**: gh-916 [IMPL] #910: route test-automation status moves/gates through stage-label fallback (backward compatible)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-916` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 49
- **Additions**: +1533
- **Deletions**: -154
- **Created**: 2026-10-16T11:58:29Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-16T12:33:53Z

## PR Description

Closes #916
### Root Cause

On restricted workflows (ADO Test Case / ADO PBI), the test-automation statuses (`Passed`, `Failed`, `In Review - Passed/Failed`, `Skipped`, `Irrelevant`, `Bug To Fix`, `In Testing`, `Ready For Testing`, `Merged`) are tag-only. ~25 modules moved tickets with raw `tracker.moveToStatus(...)`, so ADO rejected the transition and the call sites swallowed the error — no status change, no `stage_*` marker, and `✅ Moved …` logs that lied. The shipped SM rules made it worse: their JQL gated on the same statuses, so tickets carrying only a `stage_*` marker were invisible, and `smAgent`'s `rule.targetStatus` move (Merged → Ready For Testing) hit the same raw call.

### Fix

- `js/common/trackers.js`: added `hasStage(ticket, stageKey, statusName)` — status match, or (label mode only) the `stage_<key>` marker; no label reads in the default `'none'` mode.
- Migrated every test-automation mover to `moveToStatusOrMark(key, STATUS, STAGE_KEY)` (`moveToInTesting`, `moveToReadyForTesting`, `post*Results`, `mergeStoryTestAutomationPR`, `retryMergePR`, `prepareTestPRForReview`, `check*Passed`, `checkBugToFixReady`, `checkTaskStoriesDone`, `finishTestCasesGeneration`, `storyTestAutomationRework`, `triggerBitriseTestAutomation`, `recover*`, `postBugCreation`, `postBulkBugsCreation`, `createBugFixBatchEpic`); dev-flow statuses (Done, Blocked, In Rework, In Review, Backlog, …) stay direct moves.
- Status-equality gates in the check/merge/PR modules now resolve through `hasStage(...)`.
- `sm.json` (≡ `agents/sm.json`), `agents/sm_merge.json`, `agents/bulk_bugs_creation.json`: tag-only-status gates switched to whole-clause `{stage.X:Literal}` placeholders; in `'none'` mode single-status rules expand byte-identical, two-status rules to the equivalent `status in ('A') OR status in ('B')`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rule.targetStatus` resolves against the tag-only stage set and falls back to `moveToStatusOrMark`; `js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js` mirrors `testRunner.js`'s `makeDefaultConfigLoaderMock` helpers.

Opt-in via the existing `jira.stageFallback: 'label'` / `customParams.stageFallback`; default `'none'` keeps today's behaviour.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests per flow: rejected transitions in `'label'` mode now mark `stage_*` and the flow completes (e.g. `test_moveToInTesting`, `test_mergeStoryTestAutomationPR`, `test_retryMergePR`, `test_recoverMergedPRTicket`, `test_smAgent` targetStatus suites); `'none'`-mode tests pin the unchanged path.
- Full suite: 136 files from `run_all.json` — 2823 passed, 18 failed; all 18 verified pre-existing node-harness mock gaps (they fail identically at the pre-change commit `e48129c`, e.g. `file_list`/`assert.doesNotThrow` exist only in the GraalJS runner). No new failures; two `finishTestCasesGeneration` tests that already failed at `e48129c` now pass.

### Notes

- `agents/` here is a self-symlink (consumer-layout shim, gitignored) — `sm.json` and `agents/sm.json` are one file.
- Two-status `{stage.*}` rules expand to two OR-ed clauses instead of one two-value `status in (...)` — same selection, different bytes, in `'none'` mode too.
- One pre-existing node-harness failure in `test_smAgent.js` (`assert.doesNotThrow` exists only in the GraalJS runner) is unrelated.

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

The repo's own pre-existing fixture shape agrees: `makeTc()` in `test_checkBugTestsPassed.js` has no `labels`. ```javascript
function findDirectLinkedTCs(ticket) {
    // ... existing stub collection ...
    if (tracker.stageFallback() === 'label' && tcs.length > 0) {
        return tcs.map(function (tc) {
            try { return tracker.getIssue(tc.key) || tc; } catch (e) { return tc; }
        });
    }
    return tcs;
}
```

And extend the gh-916 suite with a case whose mock returns the realistic label-less stub so the fallback is exercised.

# gh-916: [IMPL] #910: route test-automation status moves/gates through stage-label fallback (backward compatible)

## Description

Implements #910, building on #907 (PR #914 — `moveToStatusOrMark` now sweeps every stale `stage_*` label, so `previousStageKey` is optional).

## Goal
On trackers whose workflow does not contain a Jira-style status (ADO Test Case: `Design`/`Ready`/`Closed`; PBI/Bug: `New`…`Done`), the test-automation pipeline must not silently no-op. Status moves must fall back to a `stage_<key>` label when `jira.stageFallback === 'label'`, and every gate/query that reads those statuses must also accept the label.

## Hard requirement: backward compatibility
- Default `stageFallback: 'none'` (and Jira/GitHub with real statuses): **identical behaviour and API calls as today** — same `moveToStatus` error handling, same JQL/WIQL text, no extra reads.
- No signature/return-shape changes of exported functions; existing config keys keep working; new behaviour is opt-in via `jira.stageFallback: 'label'` (already the existing switch).
- Existing unit tests must stay green unchanged except where they assert the old direct `moveToStatus` call — update those minimally.

## Plan (do it in small commits)
1. Add to `js/common/trackers.js` a helper `tracker.hasStage(ticket, stageKey, statusName)` → true when `ticket.status === statusName` **or** (label mode) the ticket carries `stageLabel(stageKey)`. No behaviour change in `'none'` mode.
2. blocks.text:
name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json

# Quality gate — CRAP ratchet via crap4js, pinned like crap4dart in dmd.
