blocks.text:
name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json

# Quality gate — CRAP ratchet via crap4js, pinned like crap4dart in dmd.
#
# Threshold policy (owner 2026-09-28): the CRAP bar is NOT lowered to pass —
# the CURRENT measured maximum is fixed as the ratchet baseline, so the code
# can only improve. Baseline: 4879.8 (action/developTicketAndCreatePR.js,
# CC=116 @ 29.3% coverage). Improvements lower the max freely; any change
# that pushes the max ABOVE the baseline fails the gate.
#
# Tool pin: crap4js v0.8.1 by release tag (same discipline as dmd pinning
# crap4dart 0.9.5). Install from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js' package is an
# unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  # Ratchet baseline — the measured repo-wide maximum CRAP (see header).
  # Re-measure with the steps below; lower it when the code improves.
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '4879.8'
  CRAP4JS_REF: 'v0.8.1'

jobs:
  crap:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul

pack_require_gate.cjs

blocks.text:
name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json

# Quality gate — CRAP ratchet via crap4js, pinned like crap4dart in dmd.
#
# Threshold policy (owner 2026-09-28): the CRAP bar is NOT lowered to pass —
# the CURRENT measured maximum is fixed as the ratchet baseline, so the code
# can only improve. Baseline: 4879.8 (action/developTicketAndCreatePR.js,
# CC=116 @ 29.3% coverage). Improvements lower the max freely; any change
# that pushes the max ABOVE the baseline fails the gate.
#
# Tool pin: crap4js v0.8.1 by release tag (same discipline as dmd pinning
# crap4dart 0.9.5). Install from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js' package is an
# unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  # Ratchet baseline — the measured repo-wide maximum CRAP (see header).
  # Re-measure with the steps below; lower it when the code improves.
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '4879.8'
  CRAP4JS_REF: 'v0.8.1'

jobs:
  crap:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |

# Quality gate — CRAP ratchet via crap4js, pinned like crap4dart in dmd.
#
# Threshold policy (owner 2026-09-28): the CRAP bar is NOT lowered to pass —
# the CURRENT measured maximum is fixed as the ratchet baseline, so the code
# can only improve. Baseline: 4879.8 (action/developTicketAndCreatePR.js,
# CC=116 @ 29.3% coverage). Improvements lower the max freely; any change
# that pushes the max ABOVE the baseline fails the gate.
#
# Tool pin: crap4js v0.8.1 by release tag (same discipline as dmd pinning
# crap4dart 0.9.5). Install from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js' package is an
# unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  # Ratchet baseline — the measured repo-wide maximum CRAP (see header).
  # Re-measure with the steps below; lower it when the code improves.
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '4879.8'
  CRAP4JS_REF: 'v0.8.1'

jobs:
  crap:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul

Now let me set up my task plan. The open review threads requiring fixes:

**Thread 1 (BLOCKING, `PRRT_kwDORYAuYs6tMqV5`)**: Regenerate `docs/agents/generated/bulk_bugs_creation.md` via `node js/agentDocGenerator.js`.

**Thread 2 (BLOCKING, `PRRT_kwDORYAuYs6tMqZf`)**: `findDirectLinkedTCs` in `js/checkBugTestsPassed.js` — re-fetch TCs in label mode; add test with realistic label-less stub.

**Thread 4 (SUGGESTION, `PRRT_kwDORYAuYs6tMqgV`)**: `stageKeyForStatusName` configured-status projects. Options: match against configured statuses too, or document. The suggestion says "resolve rule.targetStatus against configured statuses too". 

Hmm, think about thread 4 carefully. `stageKeyForStatusName(statusName)` looks up the DEFAULT `statuses` map (from projectConfig.jira.statuses — wait, what is projectConfig here? Let me check: `var statuses = (projectConfig && projectConfig.jira && projectConfig.jira.statuses) || {}`. So it reads the merged project config statuses. A project that customizes `jira.statuses.READY_FOR_TESTING: 'ReadyForTest'` gets `statuses['READY_FOR_TESTING'] = 'ReadyForTest'`, and sm.json's literal `targetStatus: "Ready For Testing"` no longer matches — returns null → plain move → on a restricted workflow, rejected with only a generic warn.

Wait, but how do the default statuses look? Let me check config.js STATUSES. The defaults are like `READY_FOR_TESTING: 'Ready For Testing'`. With `useConfiguredStatusesInQueries: true`, queries use configured values. If a project renames the status to 'ReadyForTest', then the sm.json rule's `targetStatus: 'Ready For Testing'` is stale even in the plain-move world — the move itself would fail ("Ready For Testing" doesn't exist in that project). Hmm, but the reviewer says "keeps the sm.json literal targetStatus: 'Ready For Testing', so the reverse lookup returns null and the SM falls back to a plain moveToStatus — on a restricted workflow the transition is rejected again".

Options given: (a) also try a case-insensitive match on the key-derived name; (b) document in sm.json that targetStatus must stay aligned with jira.statuses values when stage fallback is enabled.

What's the cheapest, safest fix that addresses the suggestion without scope creep? The reviewer marked it SUGGESTION ("Pre-existing behaviour, no regression"). Options:

Option A: Extend `stageKeyForStatusName` to fall back to the DEFAULT statuses from config.js when the configured lookup misses. I.e., match against `STATUSES[key]` (default names) too. That means for a configured-status project with `READY_FOR_TESTING: 'ReadyForTest'`, `stageKeyForStatusName('Ready For Testing')` returns 'READY_FOR_TESTING' via the default-name match, and the SM calls `moveToStatusOrMark(key, 'Ready For Testing', 'READY_FOR_TESTING')`. In label mode, if the transition of 'Ready For Testing' fails, the marker `stage_ready_for_testing` is written. The gate code that reads this stage would use configured status names + the stage key — hmm, but the SM JQL gates use `{stage.X:Literal}` placeholders which resolve to configured values... The mismatch: the marker says READY_FOR_TESTING stage, but the ticket is intended for the project's 'ReadyForTest' status which the SM rule selects via `{stage.READY_FOR_TESTING:ReadyForTest}`... wait no. Let me check how `{stage.X:Literal}` placeholders interpolate: `stage.X` resolves the configured status name X for stage key X. So the JQL would be `status = 'ReadyForTest' OR labels = 'stage_ready_for_testing'`. So even if the move itself fails with the wrong literal name, the marker lands and the ticket remains selectable. That's the improvement the fallback provides: the ticket doesn't vanish from the pipeline.

But hold on — would matching default names when configured names differ cause a WRONG move? # Quality gate — CRAP ratchet via crap4js, pinned like crap4dart in dmd.
#
# Threshold policy (owner 2026-09-28): the CRAP bar is NOT lowered to pass —
# the CURRENT measured maximum is fixed as the ratchet baseline, so the code
# can only improve. Baseline: 4879.8 (action/developTicketAndCreatePR.js,
# CC=116 @ 29.3% coverage). Improvements lower the max freely; any change
# that pushes the max ABOVE the baseline fails the gate.
#
# Tool pin: crap4js v0.8.1 by release tag (same discipline as dmd pinning
# crap4dart 0.9.5). Install from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js' package is an
# unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  # Ratchet baseline — the measured repo-wide maximum CRAP (see header).
  # Re-measure with the steps below; lower it when the code improves.
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '4879.8'
  CRAP4JS_REF: 'v0.8.1'

jobs:
  crap:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul

pack_require_gate.cjs

# Quality gate — CRAP ratchet via crap4js, pinned like crap4dart in dmd.
#
# Threshold policy (owner 2026-09-28): the CRAP bar is NOT lowered to pass —
# the CURRENT measured maximum is fixed as the ratchet baseline, so the code
# can only improve. Baseline: 4879.8 (action/developTicketAndCreatePR.js,
# CC=116 @ 29.3% coverage). Improvements lower the max freely; any change
# that pushes the max ABOVE the baseline fails the gate.
#
# Tool pin: crap4js v0.8.1 by release tag (same discipline as dmd pinning
# crap4dart 0.9.5). Install from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js' package is an
# unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  # Ratchet baseline — the measured repo-wide maximum CRAP (see header).
  # Re-measure with the steps below; lower it when the code improves.
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '4879.8'
  CRAP4JS_REF: 'v0.8.1'

jobs:
  crap:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul

Hmm, think about thread 4 carefully. `stageKeyForStatusName(statusName)` looks up the DEFAULT `statuses` map (from projectConfig.jira.statuses — wait, what is projectConfig here? Let me check: `var statuses = (projectConfig && projectConfig.jira && projectConfig.jira.statuses) || {}`. So it reads the merged project config statuses. A project that customizes `jira.statuses.READY_FOR_TESTING: 'ReadyForTest'` gets `statuses['READY_FOR_TESTING'] = 'ReadyForTest'`, and sm.json's literal `targetStatus: "Ready For Testing"` no longer matches — returns null → plain move → on a restricted workflow, rejected with only a generic warn.

Wait, but how do the default statuses look? Let me check config.js STATUSES. The defaults are like `READY_FOR_TESTING: 'Ready For Testing'`. # Quality gate — CRAP ratchet via crap4js, pinned like crap4dart in dmd.
#
# Threshold policy (owner 2026-09-28): the CRAP bar is NOT lowered to pass —
# the CURRENT measured maximum is fixed as the ratchet baseline, so the code
# can only improve. Baseline: 4879.8 (action/developTicketAndCreatePR.js,
# CC=116 @ 29.3% coverage). Improvements lower the max freely; any change
# that pushes the max ABOVE the baseline fails the gate.
#
# Tool pin: crap4js v0.8.1 by release tag (same discipline as dmd pinning
# crap4dart 0.9.5). Install from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js' package is an
# unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  # Ratchet baseline — the measured repo-wide maximum CRAP (see header).
  # Re-measure with the steps below; lower it when the code improves.
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '4879.8'
  CRAP4JS_REF: 'v0.8.1'

jobs:
  crap:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul

pack_load_probe.cjs
pack_release_guard.cjs
pack_require_gate.cjs
pack_version_guard.cjs

# Quality gate — CRAP ratchet via crap4js, pinned like crap4dart in dmd.
#
# Threshold policy (owner 2026-09-28): the CRAP bar is NOT lowered to pass —
# the CURRENT measured maximum is fixed as the ratchet baseline, so the code
# can only improve. Baseline: 4879.8 (action/developTicketAndCreatePR.js,
# CC=116 @ 29.3% coverage). Improvements lower the max freely; any change
# that pushes the max ABOVE the baseline fails the gate.
#
# Tool pin: crap4js v0.8.1 by release tag (same discipline as dmd pinning
# crap4dart 0.9.5). Install from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js' package is an
# unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  # Ratchet baseline — the measured repo-wide maximum CRAP (see header).
  # Re-measure with the steps below; lower it when the code improves.
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '4879.8'
  CRAP4JS_REF: 'v0.8.1'

jobs:
  crap:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul

Let me check: `var statuses = (projectConfig && projectConfig.jira && projectConfig.jira.statuses) || {}`. So it reads the merged project config statuses. A project that customizes `jira.statuses.READY_FOR_TESTING: 'ReadyForTest'` gets `statuses['READY_FOR_TESTING'] = 'ReadyForTest'`, and sm.json's literal `targetStatus: "Ready For Testing"` no longer matches — returns null → plain move → on a restricted workflow, rejected with only a generic warn.

Wait, but how do the default statuses look? Let me check config.js STATUSES. The defaults are like `READY_FOR_TESTING: 'Ready For Testing'`. With `useConfiguredStatusesInQueries: true`, queries use configured values. If a project renames the status to 'ReadyForTest', then the sm.json rule's `targetStatus: 'Ready For Testing'` is stale even in the plain-move world — the move itself would fail ("Ready For Testing" doesn't exist in that project). Hmm, but the reviewer says "keeps the sm.json literal targetStatus: 'Ready For Testing', so the reverse lookup returns null and the SM falls back to a plain moveToStatus — on a restricted workflow the transition is rejected again".

Options given: (a) also try a case-insensitive match on the key-derived name; (b) document in sm.json that targetStatus must stay aligned with jira.statuses values when stage fallback is enabled.

What's the cheapest, safest fix that addresses the suggestion without scope creep? The reviewer marked it SUGGESTION ("Pre-existing behaviour, no regression"). Options:

Option A: Extend `stageKeyForStatusName` to fall back to the DEFAULT statuses from config.js when the configured lookup misses. I.e., match against `STATUSES[key]` (default names) too. That means for a configured-status project with `READY_FOR_TESTING: 'ReadyForTest'`, `stageKeyForStatusName('Ready For Testing')` returns 'READY_FOR_TESTING' via the default-name match, and the SM calls `moveToStatusOrMark(key, 'Ready For Testing', 'READY_FOR_TESTING')`. In label mode, if the transition of 'Ready For Testing' fails, the marker `stage_ready_for_testing` is written. The gate code that reads this stage would use configured status names + the stage key — hmm, but the SM JQL gates use `{stage.X:Literal}` placeholders which resolve to configured values... The mismatch: the marker says READY_FOR_TESTING stage, but the ticket is intended for the project's 'ReadyForTest' status which the SM rule selects via `{stage.READY_FOR_TESTING:ReadyForTest}`... wait no. Let me check how `{stage.X:Literal}` placeholders interpolate: `stage.X` resolves the configured status name X for stage key X. So the JQL would be `status = 'ReadyForTest' OR labels = 'stage_ready_for_testing'`. So even if the move itself fails with the wrong literal name, the marker lands and the ticket remains selectable. That's the improvement the fallback provides: the ticket doesn't vanish from the pipeline.

But hold on — would matching default names when configured names differ cause a WRONG move? In a configured-status project, `targetStatus: 'Ready For Testing'` is the sm.json literal; if the project renamed the status, that move was ALREADY failing pre-PR (plain moveToStatus of a non-existent status). Adding the marker fallback makes the failure visible/recoverable rather than silent. It doesn't break anything that worked before: default-name matching only kicks in when the configured-name match missed.

Hmm, but is that the right semantic? `stageKeyForStatusName` is used in `moveStatus` to decide plain-move vs moveToStatusOrMark. With the default-name fallback, a move to a default-named status that the project has customized becomes a markable move in label mode. That matches the intent: "restricted to the test-automation stage set".

Option B (cheaper): document in sm.json. But sm.json is the SM config consumed by the product repo — adding a comment... JSON doesn't have comments. The rules are in a JSON array; there's a `description` field per rule. Documenting inside sm.json rule descriptions is odd. Alternatively document in the PR description / README. The suggestion offers "or document".

Given the TDD directive ("NEVER change production code in response to a review comment without a test that first reproduces it") and that the reviewer's preferred option is the code change ("Options: also try a case-insensitive match on the *key-derived* name, or document..."), I'll implement the code fix: `stageKeyForStatusName` falls back to matching the DEFAULT status names (case-sensitive, same as today) when the configured map doesn't match. That's basically the default name. The default STATUSES map gives exactly that mapping.

I think the cleanest fix consistent with the codebase: in `stageKeyForStatusName`, first match configured `projectConfig.jira.statuses` (as today), then fall back to the default `STATUSES` map from `js/config.js`. This makes `stageKeyForStatusName('Ready For Testing')` resolve even when the project overrode `statuses.READY_FOR_TESTING = 'ReadyForTest'`.

Wait — but hold on. Would this change behavior for projects that did NOT override statuses? `projectConfig.jira.statuses` — is it always fully populated with defaults? Let me check config.js STATUSES and how projectConfig.jira.statuses is composed. If projectConfig.jira.statuses is already the merged view (defaults + overrides), then the current lookup already matches default names for non-customizing projects, and the fallback to STATUSES only matters when an override changed the name. In that case there could be a conflict: which wins? Configured name match wins (first), then default. That's exactly the desired precedence.

But one more subtlety: what if a project sets `READY_FOR_TESTING: 'ReadyForTest'` — then `stageKeyForStatusName('ReadyForTest')` matches configured; `stageKeyForStatusName('Ready For Testing')` now ALSO returns 'READY_FOR_TESTING' via the default fallback. Let me look at the sm.json rules and interpolateStagePlaceholders to make sure the fallback logic aligns. # Quality gate — CRAP ratchet via crap4js, pinned like crap4dart in dmd.

# Threshold policy (owner 2026-09-28): the CRAP bar is NOT lowered to pass —
# the CURRENT measured maximum is fixed as the ratchet baseline, so the code
# can only improve. Baseline: 4879.8 (action/developTicketAndCreatePR.js,
# CC=116 @ 29.3% coverage). Improvements lower the max freely; any change
# that pushes the max ABOVE the baseline fails the gate.
#
# Tool pin: crap4js v0.8.1 by release tag (same discipline as dmd pinning
# crap4dart 0.9.5). Install from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js' package is an
# unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  # Ratchet baseline — the measured repo-wide maximum CRAP (see header).
  # Re-measure with the steps below; lower it when the code improves.
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '4879.8'
  CRAP4JS_REF: 'v0.8.1'

jobs:
  crap:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.

Let me check: `var statuses = (projectConfig && projectConfig.jira && projectConfig.jira.statuses) || {}`. So it reads the merged project config statuses. A project that customizes `jira.statuses.READY_FOR_TESTING: 'ReadyForTest'` gets `statuses['READY_FOR_TESTING'] = 'ReadyForTest'`, and sm.json's literal `targetStatus: "Ready For Testing"` no longer matches — returns null → plain move → on a restricted workflow, rejected with only a generic warn.

Wait, but how do the default statuses look? Let me check config.js STATUSES. The defaults are like `READY_FOR_TESTING: 'Ready For Testing'`. With `useConfiguredStatusesInQueries: true`, queries use configured values. If a project renames the status to 'ReadyForTest', then the sm.json rule's `targetStatus: 'Ready For Testing'` is stale even in the plain-move world — the move itself would fail ("Ready For Testing" doesn't exist in that project). Options given: (a) also try a case-insensitive match on the key-derived name; (b) document in sm.json that targetStatus must stay aligned with jira.statuses values when stage fallback is enabled.

What's the cheapest, safest fix that addresses the suggestion without scope creep? The reviewer marked it SUGGESTION ("Pre-existing behaviour, no regression"). Options:

Option A: Extend `stageKeyForStatusName` to fall back to the DEFAULT statuses from config.js when the configured lookup misses. I.e., match against `STATUSES[key]` (default names) too. That means for a configured-status project with `READY_FOR_TESTING: 'ReadyForTest'`, `stageKeyForStatusName('Ready For Testing')` returns 'READY_FOR_TESTING' via the default-name match, and the SM calls `moveToStatusOrMark(key, 'Ready For Testing', 'READY_FOR_TESTING')`. In label mode, if the transition of 'Ready For Testing' fails, the marker `stage_ready_for_testing` is written. The gate code that reads this stage would use configured status names + the stage key — hmm, but the SM JQL gates use `{stage.X:Literal}` placeholders which resolve to configured values... Let me check how `{stage.X:Literal}` placeholders interpolate: `stage.X` resolves the configured status name X for stage key X. So the JQL would be `status = 'ReadyForTest' OR labels = 'stage_ready_for_testing'`. So even if the move itself fails with the wrong literal name, the marker lands and the ticket remains selectable. That's the improvement the fallback provides: the ticket doesn't vanish from the pipeline.

But hold on — would matching default names when configured names differ cause a WRONG move? In a configured-status project, `targetStatus: 'Ready For Testing'` is the sm.json literal; if the project renamed the status, that move was ALREADY failing pre-PR (plain moveToStatus of a non-existent status). Adding the marker fallback makes the failure visible/recoverable rather than silent. It doesn't break anything that worked before: default-name matching only kicks in when the configured-name match missed.

# Quality gate — CRAP ratchet via crap4js, pinned like crap4dart in dmd.
#
# Threshold policy (owner 2026-09-28): the CRAP bar is NOT lowered to pass —
# the CURRENT measured maximum is fixed as the ratchet baseline, so the code
# can only improve. Baseline: 4879.8 (action/developTicketAndCreatePR.js,
# CC=116 @ 29.3% coverage). Improvements lower the max freely; any change
# that pushes the max ABOVE the baseline fails the gate.
#
# Tool pin: crap4js v0.8.1 by release tag (same discipline as dmd pinning
# crap4dart 0.9.5). Install from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js' package is an
# unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  # Ratchet baseline — the measured repo-wide maximum CRAP (see header).
  # Re-measure with the steps below; lower it when the code improves.
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '4879.8'
  CRAP4JS_REF: 'v0.8.1'

jobs:
  crap:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul

pack_require_gate.cjs
pack_version_guard.cjs

The self-symlink `agents/` was missing (it's gitignored, so a fresh checkout doesn't have it). I created it. Tests pass now.

Now let me set up my task plan. The open review threads requiring fixes:

**Thread 1 (BLOCKING, `PRRT_kwDORYAuYs6tMqV5`)**: Regenerate `docs/agents/generated/bulk_bugs_creation.md` via `node js/agentDocGenerator.js`.

**Thread 2 (BLOCKING, `PRRT_kwDORYAuYs6tMqZf`)**: `findDirectLinkedTCs` in `js/checkBugTestsPassed.js` — re-fetch TCs in label mode; add test with realistic label-less stub.

**Thread 3 (SUGGESTION, `PRRT_kwDORYAuYs6tMqch`)**: Add `run_moveToInTesting.json` + `run_moveToReadyForTesting.json`. Cheap — do it.

**Thread 4 (SUGGESTION, `PRRT_kwDORYAuYs6tMqgV`)**: `stageKeyForStatusName` configured-status projects. Options: match against configured statuses too, or document. The suggestion says "resolve rule.targetStatus against configured statuses too". 

Hmm, think about thread 4 carefully. `stageKeyForStatusName(statusName)` looks up the DEFAULT `statuses` map (from projectConfig.jira.statuses — wait, what is projectConfig here? Let me check: `var statuses = (projectConfig && projectConfig.jira && projectConfig.jira.statuses) || {}`. So it reads the merged project config statuses. A project that customizes `jira.statuses.READY_FOR_TESTING: 'ReadyForTest'` gets `statuses['READY_FOR_TESTING'] = 'ReadyForTest'`, and sm.json's literal `targetStatus: "Ready For Testing"` no longer matches — returns null → plain move → on a restricted workflow, rejected with only a generic warn.

Wait, but how do the default statuses look? Let me check config.js STATUSES. The defaults are like `READY_FOR_TESTING: 'Ready For Testing'`. With `useConfiguredStatusesInQueries: true`, queries use configured values. If a project renames the status to 'ReadyForTest', then the sm.json rule's `targetStatus: 'Ready For Testing'` is stale even in the plain-move world — the move itself would fail ("Ready For Testing" doesn't exist in that project). Hmm, but the reviewer says "keeps the sm.json literal targetStatus: 'Ready For Testing', so the reverse lookup returns null and the SM falls back to a plain moveToStatus — on a restricted workflow the transition is rejected again".

Options given: (a) also try a case-insensitive match on the key-derived name; (b) document in sm.json that targetStatus must stay aligned with jira.statuses values when stage fallback is enabled.

What's the cheapest, safest fix that addresses the suggestion without scope creep? The reviewer marked it SUGGESTION ("Pre-existing behaviour, no regression"). Options:

Option A: Extend `stageKeyForStatusName` to fall back to the DEFAULT statuses from config.js when the configured lookup misses. I.e., match against `STATUSES[key]` (default names) too. That means for a configured-status project with `READY_FOR_TESTING: 'ReadyForTest'`, `stageKeyForStatusName('Ready For Testing')` returns 'READY_FOR_TESTING' via the default-name match, and the SM calls `moveToStatusOrMark(key, 'Ready For Testing', 'READY_FOR_TESTING')`. In label mode, if the transition of 'Ready For Testing' fails, the marker `stage_ready_for_testing` is written. The gate code that reads this stage would use configured status names + the stage key — hmm, but the SM JQL gates use `{stage.X:Literal}` placeholders which resolve to configured values... The mismatch: the marker says READY_FOR_TESTING stage, but the ticket is intended for the project's 'ReadyForTest' status which the SM rule selects via `{stage.READY_FOR_TESTING:ReadyForTest}`... wait no. Let me check how `{stage.X:Literal}` placeholders interpolate: `stage.X` resolves the configured status name X for stage key X. So the JQL would be `status = 'ReadyForTest' OR labels = 'stage_ready_for_testing'`. So even if the move itself fails with the wrong literal name, the marker lands and the ticket remains selectable. That's the improvement the fallback provides: the ticket doesn't vanish from the pipeline.

But hold on — would matching default names when configured names differ cause a WRONG move? In a configured-status project, `targetStatus: 'Ready For Testing'` is the sm.json literal; if the project renamed the status, that move was ALREADY failing pre-PR (plain moveToStatus of a non-existent status). Adding the marker fallback makes the failure visible/recoverable rather than silent. It doesn't break anything that worked before: default-name matching only kicks in when the configured-name match missed.

Hmm, but is that the right semantic? `stageKeyForStatusName` is used in `moveStatus` to decide plain-move vs moveToStatusOrMark. With the default-name fallback, a move to a default-named status that the project has customized becomes a markable move in label mode. That matches the intent: "restricted to the test-automation stage set".

Option B (cheaper): document in sm.json. But sm.json is the SM config consumed by the product repo — adding a comment... JSON doesn't have comments. The rules are in a JSON array; there's a `description` field per rule. Documenting inside sm.json rule descriptions is odd. Alternatively document in the PR description / README. The suggestion offers "or document".

Given the TDD directive ("NEVER change production code in response to a review comment without a test that first reproduces it") and that the reviewer's preferred option is the code change ("Options: also try a case-insensitive match on the *key-derived* name, or document..."), I'll implement the code fix: `stageKeyForStatusName` falls back to matching the DEFAULT status names (case-sensitive, same as today) when the configured map doesn't match. Actually let me re-read: "also try a case-insensitive match on the *key-derived* name". Key-derived name — from the key 'READY_FOR_TESTING' derive 'Ready For Testing'? That's basically the default name. The default STATUSES map gives exactly that mapping.

I think the cleanest fix consistent with the codebase: in `stageKeyForStatusName`, first match configured `projectConfig.jira.statuses` (as today), then fall back to the default `STATUSES` map from `js/config.js`. This makes `stageKeyForStatusName('Ready For Testing')` resolve even when the project overrode `statuses.READY_FOR_TESTING = 'ReadyForTest'`.

Wait — but hold on. Would this change behavior for projects that did NOT override statuses? `projectConfig.jira.statuses` — is it always fully populated with defaults? `getIssue(key)` calls `jira_get_ticket({key})` and wraps in `_jiraView`. Note: `getTicket` also calls `jiraGetTicket`. So both use `jira_get_ticket` global. # Quality gate — CRAP ratchet via crap4js, pinned like crap4dart in dmd.
#
# Threshold policy (owner 2026-09-28): the CRAP bar is NOT lowered to pass —
# the CURRENT measured maximum is fixed as the ratchet baseline, so the code
# can only improve. Baseline: 4879.8 (action/developTicketAndCreatePR.js,
# CC=116 @ 29.3% coverage). Improvements lower the max freely; any change
# that pushes the max ABOVE the baseline fails the gate.
#
# Tool pin: crap4js v0.8.1 by release tag (same discipline as dmd pinning
# crap4dart 0.9.5). Install from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js' package is an
# unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  # Ratchet baseline — the measured repo-wide maximum CRAP (see header).
  # Re-measure with the steps below; lower it when the code improves.
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '4879.8'
  CRAP4JS_REF: 'v0.8.1'

jobs:
  crap:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
pack_launch_contract.cjs
pack_load_probe.cjs
pack_release_guard.cjs
pack_require_gate.cjs
pack_version_guard.cjs
release_kicker.mjs
release_kicker_guard.cjs
release_packs.mjs
run_with_coverage.js

name: Quality

on:

jobs:

# Quality gate — CRAP ratchet via crap4js, pinned like crap4dart in dmd.
#
# Threshold policy (owner 2026-09-28): the CRAP bar is NOT lowered to pass —
# the CURRENT measured maximum is fixed as the ratchet baseline, so the code
# can only improve. Baseline: 4879.8 (action/developTicketAndCreatePR.js,
# CC=116 @ 29.3% coverage). Improvements lower the max freely; any change
# that pushes the max ABOVE the baseline fails the gate.
#
# Tool pin: crap4js v0.8.1 by release tag (same discipline as dmd pinning
# crap4dart 0.9.5). Install from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js' package is an
# unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  # Ratchet baseline — the measured repo-wide maximum CRAP (see header).
  # Re-measure with the steps below; lower it when the code improves.
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '4879.8'
  CRAP4JS_REF: 'v0.8.1'

jobs:
  crap:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.

# Quality gate — CRAP ratchet via crap4js, pinned like crap4dart in dmd.
#
# Threshold policy (owner 2026-09-28): the CRAP bar is NOT lowered to pass —
# the CURRENT measured maximum is fixed as the ratchet baseline, so the code
# can only improve. Baseline: 4879.8 (action/developTicketAndCreatePR.js,
# CC=116 @ 29.3% coverage). Improvements lower the max freely; any change
# that pushes the max ABOVE the baseline fails the gate.
#
# Tool pin: crap4js v0.8.1 by release tag (same discipline as dmd pinning
# crap4dart 0.9.5). Install from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js' package is an
# unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  # Ratchet baseline — the measured repo-wide maximum CRAP (see header).
  # Re-measure with the steps below; lower it when the code improves.
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '4879.8'
  CRAP4JS_REF: 'v0.8.1'

jobs:
  crap:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
pack_launch_contract.cjs
pack_load_probe.cjs
pack_release_guard.cjs
pack_require_gate.cjs
pack_version_guard.cjs
release_kicker.mjs
release_kicker_guard.cjs
release_packs.mjs
run_with_coverage.js

Let me check: `var statuses = (projectConfig && projectConfig.jira && projectConfig.jira.statuses) || {}`. So it reads the merged project config statuses. A project that customizes `jira.statuses.READY_FOR_TESTING: 'ReadyForTest'` gets `statuses['READY_FOR_TESTING'] = 'ReadyForTest'`, and sm.json's literal `targetStatus: "Ready For Testing"` no longer matches — returns null → plain move → on a restricted workflow, rejected with only a generic warn.

Wait, but how do the default statuses look? Let me check config.js STATUSES. The defaults are like `READY_FOR_TESTING: 'Ready For Testing'`. With `useConfiguredStatusesInQueries: true`, queries use configured values. If a project renames the status to 'ReadyForTest', then the sm.json rule's `targetStatus: 'Ready For Testing'` is stale even in the plain-move world — the move itself would fail ("Ready For Testing" doesn't exist in that project). Hmm, but the reviewer says "keeps the sm.json literal targetStatus: 'Ready For Testing', so the reverse lookup returns null and the SM falls back to a plain moveToStatus — on a restricted workflow the transition is rejected again".

Options given: (a) also try a case-insensitive match on the key-derived name; (b) document in sm.json that targetStatus must stay aligned with jira.statuses values when stage fallback is enabled.

What's the cheapest, safest fix that addresses the suggestion without scope creep? The reviewer marked it SUGGESTION ("Pre-existing behaviour, no regression"). Options:

Option A: Extend `stageKeyForStatusName` to fall back to the DEFAULT statuses from config.js when the configured lookup misses. I.e., match against `STATUSES[key]` (default names) too. That means for a configured-status project with `READY_FOR_TESTING: 'ReadyForTest'`, `stageKeyForStatusName('Ready For Testing')` returns 'READY_FOR_TESTING' via the default-name match, and the SM calls `moveToStatusOrMark(key, 'Ready For Testing', 'READY_FOR_TESTING')`. In label mode, if the transition of 'Ready For Testing' fails, the marker `stage_ready_for_testing` is written. The gate code that reads this stage would use configured status names + the stage key — hmm, but the SM JQL gates use `{stage.X:Literal}` placeholders which resolve to configured values... The mismatch: the marker says READY_FOR_TESTING stage, but the ticket is intended for the project's 'ReadyForTest' status which the SM rule selects via `{stage.READY_FOR_TESTING:ReadyForTest}`... wait no. Let me check how `{stage.X:Literal}` placeholders interpolate: `stage.X` resolves the configured status name X for stage key X. So the JQL would be `status = 'ReadyForTest' OR labels = 'stage_ready_for_testing'`. So even if the move itself fails with the wrong literal name, the marker lands and the ticket remains selectable. That's the improvement the fallback provides: the ticket doesn't vanish from the pipeline.

But hold on — would matching default names when configured names differ cause a WRONG move? In a configured-status project, `targetStatus: 'Ready For Testing'` is the sm.json literal; if the project renamed the status, that move was ALREADY failing pre-PR (plain moveToStatus of a non-existent status). Adding the marker fallback makes the failure visible/recoverable rather than silent. It doesn't break anything that worked before: default-name matching only kicks in when the configured-name match missed.

Hmm, but is that the right semantic? `stageKeyForStatusName` is used in `moveStatus` to decide plain-move vs moveToStatusOrMark. With the default-name fallback, a move to a default-named status that the project has customized becomes a markable move in label mode. That matches the intent: "restricted to the test-automation stage set".

Option B (cheaper): document in sm.json. But sm.json is the SM config consumed by the product repo — adding a comment... JSON doesn't have comments. The rules are in a JSON array; there's a `description` field per rule. Documenting inside sm.json rule descriptions is odd. Alternatively document in the PR description / README. The suggestion offers "or document".

Given the TDD directive ("NEVER change production code in response to a review comment without a test that first reproduces it") and that the reviewer's preferred option is the code change ("Options: also try a case-insensitive match on the *key-derived* name, or document..."), I'll implement the code fix: `stageKeyForStatusName` falls back to matching the DEFAULT status names (case-sensitive, same as today) when the configured map doesn't match. Actually let me re-read: "also try a case-insensitive match on the *key-derived* name". Key-derived name — from the key 'READY_FOR_TESTING' derive 'Ready For Testing'? That's basically the default name. The default STATUSES map gives exactly that mapping.

I think the cleanest fix consistent with the codebase: in `stageKeyForStatusName`, first match configured `projectConfig.jira.statuses` (as today), then fall back to the default `STATUSES` map from `js/config.js`. This makes `stageKeyForStatusName('Ready For Testing')` resolve even when the project overrode `statuses.READY_FOR_TESTING = 'ReadyForTest'`.

Wait — but hold on. Would this change behavior for projects that did NOT override statuses? `projectConfig.jira.statuses` — is it always fully populated with defaults? Let me check config.js STATUSES and how projectConfig.jira.statuses is composed. If projectConfig.jira.statuses is already the merged view (defaults + overrides), then the current lookup already matches default names for non-customizing projects, and the fallback to STATUSES only matters when an override changed the name. In that case there could be a conflict: which wins? Configured name match wins (first), then default. That's exactly the desired precedence.

But one more subtlety: what if a project sets `READY_FOR_TESTING: 'ReadyForTest'` — then `stageKeyForStatusName('ReadyForTest')` matches configured; `stageKeyForStatusName('Ready For Testing')` now ALSO returns 'READY_FOR_TESTING' via the default fallback. Both literals map to the same stage key. That's fine for the marker (stage key is what matters).

Also `sm.json`'s `useConfiguredStatusesInQueries: true` projects: the JQL placeholders `{stage.READY_FOR_TESTING:...}` — how does the literal work there? Let me look at the sm.json rules and interpolateStagePlaceholders to make sure the fallback logic aligns. blocks.text:
The self-symlink `agents/` was missing (it's gitignored, so a fresh checkout doesn't have it). I created it. Tests pass now.

Now let me set up my task plan. The open review threads requiring fixes:

**Thread 1 (BLOCKING, `PRRT_kwDORYAuYs6tMqV5`)**: Regenerate `docs/agents/generated/bulk_bugs_creation.md` via `node js/agentDocGenerator.js`.

**Thread 2 (BLOCKING, `PRRT_kwDORYAuYs6tMqZf`)**: `findDirectLinkedTCs` in `js/checkBugTestsPassed.js` — re-fetch TCs in label mode; add test with realistic label-less stub.

**Thread 3 (SUGGESTION, `PRRT_kwDORYAuYs6tMqch`)**: Add `run_moveToInTesting.json` + `run_moveToReadyForTesting.json`. Cheap — do it.

**Thread 4 (SUGGESTION, `PRRT_kwDORYAuYs6tMqgV`)**: `stageKeyForStatusName` configured-status projects. Options: match against configured statuses too, or document. The suggestion says "resolve rule.targetStatus against configured statuses too". 

Hmm, think about thread 4 carefully. `stageKeyForStatusName(statusName)` looks up the DEFAULT `statuses` map (from projectConfig.jira.statuses — wait, what is projectConfig here? Let me check: `var statuses = (projectConfig && projectConfig.jira && projectConfig.jira.statuses) || {}`. So it reads the merged project config statuses. A project that customizes `jira.statuses.READY_FOR_TESTING: 'ReadyForTest'` gets `statuses['READY_FOR_TESTING'] = 'ReadyForTest'`, and sm.json's literal `targetStatus: "Ready For Testing"` no longer matches — returns null → plain move → on a restricted workflow, rejected with only a generic warn.

Wait, but how do the default statuses look? Let me check config.js STATUSES. The defaults are like `READY_FOR_TESTING: 'Ready For Testing'`. With `useConfiguredStatusesInQueries: true`, queries use configured values. If a project renames the status to 'ReadyForTest', then the sm.json rule's `targetStatus: 'Ready For Testing'` is stale even in the plain-move world — the move itself would fail ("Ready For Testing" doesn't exist in that project). Hmm, but the reviewer says "keeps the sm.json literal targetStatus: 'Ready For Testing', so the reverse lookup returns null and the SM falls back to a plain moveToStatus — on a restricted workflow the transition is rejected again".

Options given: (a) also try a case-insensitive match on the key-derived name; (b) document in sm.json that targetStatus must stay aligned with jira.statuses values when stage fallback is enabled.

What's the cheapest, safest fix that addresses the suggestion without scope creep? The reviewer marked it SUGGESTION ("Pre-existing behaviour, no regression"). Options:

Option A: Extend `stageKeyForStatusName` to fall back to the DEFAULT statuses from config.js when the configured lookup misses. I.e., match against `STATUSES[key]` (default names) too. That means for a configured-status project with `READY_FOR_TESTING: 'ReadyForTest'`, `stageKeyForStatusName('Ready For Testing')` returns 'READY_FOR_TESTING' via the default-name match, and the SM calls `moveToStatusOrMark(key, 'Ready For Testing', 'READY_FOR_TESTING')`. In label mode, if the transition of 'Ready For Testing' fails, the marker `stage_ready_for_testing` is written. The gate code that reads this stage would use configured status names + the stage key — hmm, but the SM JQL gates use `{stage.X:Literal}` placeholders which resolve to configured values... The mismatch: the marker says READY_FOR_TESTING stage, but the ticket is intended for the project's 'ReadyForTest' status which the SM rule selects via `{stage.READY_FOR_TESTING:ReadyForTest}`... wait no. Let me check how `{stage.X:Literal}` placeholders interpolate: `stage.X` resolves the configured status name X for stage key X. So the JQL would be `status = 'ReadyForTest' OR labels = 'stage_ready_for_testing'`. So even if the move itself fails with the wrong literal name, the marker lands and the ticket remains selectable. That's the improvement the fallback provides: the ticket doesn't vanish from the pipeline.

But hold on — would matching default names when configured names differ cause a WRONG move? In a configured-status project, `targetStatus: 'Ready For Testing'` is the sm.json literal; if the project renamed the status, that move was ALREADY failing pre-PR (plain moveToStatus of a non-existent status). Adding the marker fallback makes the failure visible/recoverable rather than silent. It doesn't break anything that worked before: default-name matching only kicks in when the configured-name match missed.

Hmm, but is that the right semantic? `stageKeyForStatusName` is used in `moveStatus` to decide plain-move vs moveToStatusOrMark. With the default-name fallback, a move to a default-named status that the project has customized becomes a markable move in label mode. That matches the intent: "restricted to the test-automation stage set".

Option B (cheaper): document in sm.json. But sm.json is the SM config consumed by the product repo — adding a comment... JSON doesn't have comments. The rules are in a JSON array; there's a `description` field per rule. Documenting inside sm.json rule descriptions is odd. Alternatively document in the PR description / README. The suggestion offers "or document".

Given the TDD directive ("NEVER change production code in response to a review comment without a test that first reproduces it") and that the reviewer's preferred option is the code change ("Options: also try a case-insensitive match on the *key-derived* name, or document..."), I'll implement the code fix: `stageKeyForStatusName` falls back to matching the DEFAULT status names (case-sensitive, same as today) when the configured map doesn't match. Actually let me re-read: "also try a case-insensitive match on the *key-derived* name". Key-derived name — from the key 'READY_FOR_TESTING' derive 'Ready For Testing'? That's basically the default name. The default STATUSES map gives exactly that mapping.

I think the cleanest fix consistent with the codebase: in `stageKeyForStatusName`, first match configured `projectConfig.jira.statuses` (as today), then fall back to the default `STATUSES` map from `js/config.js`. This makes `stageKeyForStatusName('Ready For Testing')` resolve even when the project overrode `statuses.READY_FOR_TESTING = 'ReadyForTest'`.

Wait — but hold on. Would this change behavior for projects that did NOT override statuses? `projectConfig.jira.statuses` — is it always fully populated with defaults? Let me check config.js STATUSES and how projectConfig.jira.statuses is composed. If projectConfig.jira.statuses is already the merged view (defaults + overrides), then the current lookup already matches default names for non-customizing projects, and the fallback to STATUSES only matters when an override changed the name. In that case there could be a conflict: which wins? Configured name match wins (first), then default. That's exactly the desired precedence.

But one more subtlety: what if a project sets `READY_FOR_TESTING: 'ReadyForTest'` — then `stageKeyForStatusName('ReadyForTest')` matches configured; `stageKeyForStatusName('Ready For Testing')` now ALSO returns 'READY_FOR_TESTING' via the default fallback. Both literals map to the same stage key. That's fine for the marker (stage key is what matters).

Also `sm.json`'s `useConfiguredStatusesInQueries: true` projects: the JQL placeholders `{stage.READY_FOR_TESTING:...}` — how does the literal work there? Let me look at the sm.json rules and interpolateStagePlaceholders to make sure the fallback logic aligns. Actually the placeholder `{stage.X:Literal}`: X is the stage key, Literal is the default fallback name used when not configured? Let me check `interpolateStagePlaceholders`.

Let me also check the sm.json diff for how the rules changed.

Then thread 2's test: realistic label-less stub + re-fetch. And I need to check `test_smAgent.js` gh-916 suites for targetStatus to extend for the thread-4 change (TDD: write the failing test first).

Let me now look at sm.json's current rules and the config.js STATUSES.

With `useConfiguredStatusesInQueries: true`, queries use configured values. If a project renames the status to 'ReadyForTest', then the sm.json rule's `targetStatus: 'Ready For Testing'` is stale even in the plain-move world — the move itself would fail ("Ready For Testing" doesn't exist in that project). Options given: (a) also try a case-insensitive match on the key-derived name; (b) document in sm.json that targetStatus must stay aligned with jira.statuses values when stage fallback is enabled.

What's the cheapest, safest fix that addresses the suggestion without scope creep? The reviewer marked it SUGGESTION ("Pre-existing behaviour, no regression"). Options:

Option A: Extend `stageKeyForStatusName` to fall back to the DEFAULT statuses from config.js when the configured lookup misses. I.e., match against `STATUSES[key]` (default names) too. That means for a configured-status project with `READY_FOR_TESTING: 'ReadyForTest'`, `stageKeyForStatusName('Ready For Testing')` returns 'READY_FOR_TESTING' via the default-name match, and the SM calls `moveToStatusOrMark(key, 'Ready For Testing', 'READY_FOR_TESTING')`. In label mode, if the transition of 'Ready For Testing' fails, the marker `stage_ready_for_testing` is written. The gate code that reads this stage would use configured status names + the stage key — hmm, but the SM JQL gates use `{stage.X:Literal}` placeholders which resolve to configured values... The mismatch: the marker says READY_FOR_TESTING stage, but the ticket is intended for the project's 'ReadyForTest' status which the SM rule selects via `{stage.READY_FOR_TESTING:ReadyForTest}`... wait no. Let me check how `{stage.X:Literal}` placeholders interpolate: `stage.X` resolves the configured status name X for stage key X. So the JQL would be `status = 'ReadyForTest' OR labels = 'stage_ready_for_testing'`. So even if the move itself fails with the wrong literal name, the marker lands and the ticket remains selectable. That's the improvement the fallback provides: the ticket doesn't vanish from the pipeline.

But hold on — would matching default names when configured names differ cause a WRONG move? In a configured-status project, `targetStatus: 'Ready For Testing'` is the sm.json literal; if the project renamed the status, that move was ALREADY failing pre-PR (plain moveToStatus of a non-existent status). Adding the marker fallback makes the failure visible/recoverable rather than silent. It doesn't break anything that worked before: default-name matching only kicks in when the configured-name match missed.

Hmm, but is that the right semantic? `stageKeyForStatusName` is used in `moveStatus` to decide plain-move vs moveToStatusOrMark. With the default-name fallback, a move to a default-named status that the project has customized becomes a markable move in label mode. That matches the intent: "restricted to the test-automation stage set".

Option B (cheaper): document in sm.json. But sm.json is the SM config consumed by the product repo — adding a comment... JSON doesn't have comments. The rules are in a JSON array; there's a `description` field per rule. Documenting inside sm.json rule descriptions is odd. Alternatively document in the PR description / README. The suggestion offers "or document".

Given the TDD directive ("NEVER change production code in response to a review comment without a test that first reproduces it") and that the reviewer's preferred option is the code change ("Options: also try a case-insensitive match on the *key-derived* name, or document..."), I'll implement the code fix: `stageKeyForStatusName` falls back to matching the DEFAULT status names (case-sensitive, same as today) when the configured map doesn't match. If projectConfig.jira.statuses is already the merged view (defaults + overrides), then the current lookup already matches default names for non-customizing projects, and the fallback to STATUSES only matters when an override changed the name. **Thread 1 (BLOCKING, `PRRT_kwDORYAuYs6tMqV5`)**: Regenerate `docs/agents/generated/bulk_bugs_creation.md` via `node js/agentDocGenerator.js`.

**Thread 2 (BLOCKING, `PRRT_kwDORYAuYs6tMqZf`)**: `findDirectLinkedTCs` in `js/checkBugTestsPassed.js` — re-fetch TCs in label mode; add test with realistic label-less stub.

**Thread 4 (SUGGESTION, `PRRT_kwDORYAuYs6tMqgV`)**: `stageKeyForStatusName` configured-status projects. Options: match against configured statuses too, or document. The suggestion says "resolve rule.targetStatus against configured statuses too". 

Hmm, think about thread 4 carefully. `stageKeyForStatusName(statusName)` looks up the DEFAULT `statuses` map (from projectConfig.jira.statuses — wait, what is projectConfig here? Let me check: `var statuses = (projectConfig && projectConfig.jira && projectConfig.jira.statuses) || {}`. So it reads the merged project config statuses. A project that customizes `jira.statuses.READY_FOR_TESTING: 'ReadyForTest'` gets `statuses['READY_FOR_TESTING'] = 'ReadyForTest'`, and sm.json's literal `targetStatus: "Ready For Testing"` no longer matches — returns null → plain move → on a restricted workflow, rejected with only a generic warn.

Wait, but how do the default statuses look? Let me check config.js STATUSES. The defaults are like `READY_FOR_TESTING: 'Ready For Testing'`. With `useConfiguredStatusesInQueries: true`, queries use configured values. If a project renames the status to 'ReadyForTest', then the sm.json rule's `targetStatus: 'Ready For Testing'` is stale even in the plain-move world — the move itself would fail ("Ready For Testing" doesn't exist in that project). Hmm, but the reviewer says "keeps the sm.json literal targetStatus: 'Ready For Testing', so the reverse lookup returns null and the SM falls back to a plain moveToStatus — on a restricted workflow the transition is rejected again".

Options given: (a) also try a case-insensitive match on the key-derived name; (b) document in sm.json that targetStatus must stay aligned with jira.statuses values when stage fallback is enabled.

What's the cheapest, safest fix that addresses the suggestion without scope creep? The reviewer marked it SUGGESTION ("Pre-existing behaviour, no regression"). Options:

Option A: Extend `stageKeyForStatusName` to fall back to the DEFAULT statuses from config.js when the configured lookup misses. I.e., match against `STATUSES[key]` (default names) too. That means for a configured-status project with `READY_FOR_TESTING: 'ReadyForTest'`, `stageKeyForStatusName('Ready For Testing')` returns 'READY_FOR_TESTING' via the default-name match, and the SM calls `moveToStatusOrMark(key, 'Ready For Testing', 'READY_FOR_TESTING')`. In label mode, if the transition of 'Ready For Testing' fails, the marker `stage_ready_for_testing` is written. The gate code that reads this stage would use configured status names + the stage key — hmm, but the SM JQL gates use `{stage.X:Literal}` placeholders which resolve to configured values... The mismatch: the marker says READY_FOR_TESTING stage, but the ticket is intended for the project's 'ReadyForTest' status which the SM rule selects via `{stage.READY_FOR_TESTING:ReadyForTest}`... wait no. Let me check how `{stage.X:Literal}` placeholders interpolate: `stage.X` resolves the configured status name X for stage key X. So the JQL would be `status = 'ReadyForTest' OR labels = 'stage_ready_for_testing'`. So even if the move itself fails with the wrong literal name, the marker lands and the ticket remains selectable. That's the improvement the fallback provides: the ticket doesn't vanish from the pipeline.

But hold on — would matching default names when configured names differ cause a WRONG move? In a configured-status project, `targetStatus: 'Ready For Testing'` is the sm.json literal; if the project renamed the status, that move was ALREADY failing pre-PR (plain moveToStatus of a non-existent status). # PR Rework — gh-916 review fixes (heads after `378dfbd9`)

## Issues/Notes

- 🚨 **BLOCKING (CI `docs-freshness`)** — `docs/agents/generated/bulk_bugs_creation.md` was stale: the PR changed `failedTCsJql` in `bulk_bugs_creation.json` without regenerating the doc. Reproduced locally on `378dfbd9` (`git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` → 1), fixed by regeneration.
- 🚨 **BLOCKING** — `checkBugTestsPassed` label-mode gates could never see stage markers on the **direct-links path**: `issuelinks[].outwardIssue` stubs carry no `labels`, so `hasStage(...)` always missed there and a `stage_passed`-marked TC blocked the Bug forever. The gh-916 fixtures masked this by stuffing labels into the stubs (data the real Jira API does not return).
- 💡 **SUGGESTION** — the two new suites (`test_moveToInTesting.js`, `test_moveToReadyForTesting.js`) were only listed in `run_all.json`, missing their per-module `run_<module>.json` (AGENTS.md convention).
- 💡 **SUGGESTION** — `stageKeyForStatusName` matched configured status names only, so a project that renames a status (`jira.statuses.READY_FOR_TESTING: 'ReadyForTest'` + `useConfiguredStatusesInQueries`) silently lost the `rule.targetStatus` stage-marker fallback.
- ℹ️ Same-pattern sweep: `js/unblockResolvedDependencies.js` also reads blocker status from `issuelinks` stubs and compares against a terminal list containing `PASSED`/`IRRELEVANT`. It was deliberately **not** touched — it is pre-existing behaviour unchanged on `main`, outside this PR's migration list and not flagged in review; noted here for a future ticket.
- ℹ️ Threads without a `threadId` in `pr_discussions_raw.json` (red-gate record, automated-review record, rework-consume audit, rework-armed notice) are machine boilerplate marked "do not reply" — no reply entries were created for them.

## Approach

1. **Docs freshness** — ran `node js/agentDocGenerator.js`; only `docs/agents/generated/bulk_bugs_creation.md` drifted (exactly the diff from the review thread); `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` now exits 0.
2. **Direct-links re-fetch (TDD)** — rewrote the `checkBugTestsPassed: stage-label fallback (gh-916)` suite to the realistic shape: label-less `issuelinks` stubs, key-aware `jira_get_ticket` mock, stage labels only on the full fetch. Both label-mode tests were **red** before the change (action `waiting` instead of `moved_to_done`). Fix: when `tracker.stageFallback() === 'label'` and TCs were found, re-fetch each TC via `tracker.getIssue(tc.key)` (falling back to the stub on error); `'none'` mode keeps the stubs with zero extra reads (pinned by asserting the fetched keys are only the Bug's). Added a degradation test for a failing re-fetch.
3. **Per-module runners** — added `js/unit-tests/run_moveToInTesting.json` and `js/unit-tests/run_moveToReadyForTesting.json`, mirroring the existing one-file runner convention.
4. **Configured-status fallback (TDD)** — added a red test: renamed-status project + label mode + rejecting transition + the `sm.json` literal `targetStatus: "Ready For Testing"` → no marker (before) / `stage_ready_for_testing` (after). Fix: second resolution pass in `stageKeyForStatusName` matching the default (key-derived) status name case-insensitively, still restricted to `TAG_ONLY_STAGE_KEYS`; configured-name exact match keeps precedence. `In Development` and other dev-flow statuses still resolve to `null` → plain move.

## Files Modified

- `js/checkBugTestsPassed.js` — label-mode full re-fetch of direct-linked TCs in `findDirectLinkedTCs`.
- `js/smAgent.js` — hoisted `require('./config.js')`; `stageKeyForStatusName` second pass over the default status names.
- `js/unit-tests/test_checkBugTestsPassed.js` — realistic gh-916 fixtures + re-fetch/no-refetch/degrade assertions (11 → 14 tests).
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — `./config.js` wired into the harness require map; two new configured-status tests in the gh-916 targetStatus suite.
- `js/unit-tests/run_moveToInTesting.json`, `js/unit-tests/run_moveToReadyForTesting.json` — new per-module runners.
- `docs/agents/generated/bulk_bugs_creation.md` — regenerated (`failedTCsJql` now documents the `{stage.FAILED:Failed}` placeholder).

## Test Coverage

- New/updated tests (all red-first for the two code fixes):
  - `checkBugTestsPassed: stage-label fallback (gh-916)` — 4 tests: `'none'` mode waits with no TC re-fetch; `'label'` mode recognises `stage_passed` / `stage_bug_to_fix` **through the realistic label-less stub** (asserts the TC key was re-fetched); re-fetch failure degrades to the stub.
  - `smAgent: targetStatus stage-label fallback (gh-916)` — +2 tests: renamed configured status resolved via the default name (the literal `targetStatus` case, red before the fix); renamed status reached by its own configured name.
- Full suite (canonical runner): `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — **2889 passed, 0 failed** (baseline on `378dfbd9`: 2886 passed, 0 failed; +3 net new tests, no regressions).
- Docs gates: `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` → `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` exit 0; `run_agentDocs.json` (3 passed) and `run_agentDocsCoverage.json` (5 passed) green.
- New runners verified individually: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_moveToInTesting.json` and `run_moveToReadyForTesting.json` → 3 passed, 0 failed each.
